topic.title: Agent Registry
topic.docSection: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry & §5 Triggers #13–#14
topic.summary: 3 core goals, auto-registration vs manual writable Service resource, read-only Agent/McpServer/Endpoint, urn:agent Identifier vs principal:// IAM Principal, A2A vs standalone skills.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 15
questions.q: What is Google Cloud Agent Registry?
options: A centralized catalog that lets you store, discover, and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills, and AI agents within Google Cloud
A managed serverless container runtime that replaces Cloud Run for ADK agents
A foundation model weight repository that replaces Vertex AI Model Registry
An API gateway that terminates mTLS and bills token usage
questions.why: Verbatim doc definition (§1.4): Agent Registry is 'a centralized catalog that lets you store, discover, and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills, and AI agents within Google Cloud.' It is not a runtime or model registry.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Self-Test #3 & Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 15
questions.q: What are the three official goals of Google Cloud Agent Registry?
options: Accelerate development, simplify integration, and support governance
Host containers, fine-tune foundation models, and manage token billing
Replace Cloud IAM, encrypt VPC traffic, and redact PII
Auto-scale runtimes, cache prompts, and provision throughput
questions.why: Agent Registry's three goals (§1.4) are: (1) Accelerate development (discovery and reuse), (2) Simplify integration (standardized MCP and A2A protocols), and (3) Support governance (enforce security and boundaries across the agentic fleet).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #14 | M2S2 Slide 16
questions.q: A team deploys agents across Google Cloud. Which deployment requires MANUAL registration in Agent Registry via a writable Service resource?
options: An ADK A2A agent deployed on Cloud Run
An agent deployed on Agent Runtime (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
A GKE deployment configured with Agent Registry annotations
An official Google Cloud remote MCP server
questions.why: Auto-registration covers supported Google Cloud runtimes once the API is enabled (Agent Runtime, Workspace/Gemini Enterprise, annotated GKE, and official Google remote MCP servers). Cloud Run agents are NOT auto-discovered and require manual registration via the writable Service resource.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Self-Test #3 & Trigger #14 | M2S2 Slide 20
questions.q: When manually registering or updating an item in Agent Registry, which resource is WRITABLE versus READ-ONLY?
options: Service is writable; Agent, McpServer, and Endpoint are read-only
Agent and McpServer are writable; Service is read-only
Endpoint is writable; Service and Agent are read-only
All resources (Service, Agent, McpServer, Endpoint) are directly writable
questions.why: Everything registered manually is written through the writable 'Service' resource, and then queried through the read-only 'Agent', 'McpServer', and 'Endpoint' resources.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 (Swapped-Definition Trap) | M2S2 Slide 18
questions.q: A security engineer wants to grant an agent IAM permission to query BigQuery. Should they use the Agent Identifier or the Agent Principal?
options: Agent Principal (principal://...), because Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...) is only a logical catalog name and is never used in IAM bindings
Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...), because it is the primary IAM identity for all registered agents
Either one, because Identifier and Principal are interchangeable in IAM bindings
Neither, because agents can never hold an IAM identity for Google Cloud resources
questions.why: Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...) is a logical catalog ID used for inventory and lookup—never in IAM bindings. Agent Principal (principal://...) is the SPIFFE/service-account IAM identity used for permissions and auditing.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 19
questions.q: How do A2A skills differ from standalone skills in Agent Registry?
options: A2A skills are declarative metadata inline in an Agent Card; standalone skills are separate resources managed via Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher
A2A skills are top-level GCP resources; standalone skills only exist inline inside an Agent Card
A2A skills are for MCP servers only; standalone skills are for Cloud Run only
There is no difference; both are stored exclusively inside an Agent Card
questions.why: A2A skills are declarative metadata declared inline in an agent's Agent Card. Standalone skills are separate catalog resources managed, versioned, and listed through the Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher resources.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 17
questions.q: An orchestrator uses the Agent Registry MCP server to find agents by natural-language keyword. Which tool should it call?
options: search_agents (while list_agents enumerates by project/location, and search_mcp_servers covers MCP servers only)
search_mcp_servers, which searches both agents and MCP servers
list_agents, which performs natural-language semantic search across all projects
find_endpoints, which searches agents, tools, and skills together
questions.why: The Registry MCP server provides 'list_agents' for enumerating agents by project and location, 'search_agents' for keyword/prefix/natural-language discovery of agents, and 'search_mcp_servers' for MCP servers only.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 16
questions.q: What is the correct four-stage operating sequence in Agent Registry?
options: Register → Discover → Govern → Orchestrate
Discover → Register → Orchestrate → Govern
Govern → Register → Discover → Orchestrate
Register → Orchestrate → Discover → Govern
questions.why: The four-stage lifecycle in Agent Registry is Register → Discover → Govern → Orchestrate.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 20
questions.q: In Agent Registry, what is the difference between a Tool and an Endpoint?
options: Tools are deterministic functions served by MCP servers; Endpoints are target URLs (such as REST APIs) governed in the registry
Endpoints are deterministic functions on MCP servers; Tools are legacy REST URLs
Tools and Endpoints are two names for the exact same MCP resource
Endpoints are only for Gemini Enterprise, while Tools are only for Cloud Run
questions.why: Tools represent callable functions exposed by MCP servers, while Endpoints represent target network URLs/APIs registered for discovery and governance.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #14 | M2S2 Slide 16
questions.q: A developer publishes a Cloud Run agent to a Gemini Enterprise app, but it does not appear in Agent Registry. Why?
options: Gemini Enterprise and Agent Registry are separate catalogs that don't auto-sync for Cloud Run, so the Cloud Run agent must be registered manually via a Service resource
Agent Registry takes 24 hours to sync asynchronously from Gemini Enterprise
Cloud Run agents are blocked from being added to Agent Registry under any configuration
Agent Registry only stores MCP servers, never AI agents
questions.why: Cloud Run agents are not automatically discovered by Agent Registry and must be manually registered through the writable Service resource.
